label: integer_constants
graph_version: 3.9.8 (3.9.7 + one primary per misconception (S9c) and the four remaining sibling edges (S9b), 2026-11-04; listed in revision_3_9_8)

edges.label: [0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: 'maximum' is a ceiling that nothing can pass (like a full tank, adding more leaves it full) and an absolute value is never negative. Java rule: int arithmetic wraps around silently, so Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 is Integer.MIN_VALUE and Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is still -2147483648.

[0] names_the_element (N): Integer.MAX_VALUE and Integer.MIN_VALUE are named constants of the wrapper class Integer: the largest int, 2147483647 (2^31 - 1), and the smallest int, -2147483648 (-2^31).
[1] states_the_rule (S): Each wrapper class defines MIN_VALUE and MAX_VALUE; for int the range is -2147483648 to 2147483647 inclusive, and results outside it are truncated (wrap) without any error signal.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The constant is read like a variable when its expression is evaluated; then operators are applied in precedence order, left operand first, each in 32-bit int arithmetic, wrapping at each step that leaves the range.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Type int, value wrapped modulo 2^32: Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 is -2147483648, Integer.MIN_VALUE - 1 is 2147483647, 2 * Integer.MAX_VALUE is -2, and Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is -2147483648.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Reading the constant changes nothing (it is final); after int a = Integer.MAX_VALUE; a = a + 1; the variable a holds Integer.MIN_VALUE, and no exception is raised.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Integer.MAX_VALUE marks the overflow boundary: an int result past it wraps to a negative value, so a test such as sum > Integer.MAX_VALUE on an int is always false; an overflow guard must test before the operation (e.g. a > Integer.MAX_VALUE - b) or use long.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Used as the initial value of a most-wanted holder (Sajaniemi): max = Integer.MIN_VALUE (or min = Integer.MAX_VALUE) so the first real value always replaces it; also used as limits in overflow guards.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Changing the type from int to long moves the wrap point from 2^31 to 2^63 but does not remove it; replacing the initial max = Integer.MIN_VALUE by max = 0 breaks the search for all-negative inputs. Invariant: the range is asymmetric, Integer.MIN_VALUE == -Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1, so negating MIN_VALUE gives MIN_VALUE back.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use Integer.MAX_VALUE / MIN_VALUE as sentinels for min/max searches and as bounds in overflow checks instead of typing digits; when values can approach the limits, switch to long rather than relying on the int constants.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: int arithmetic stays within Integer.MIN_VALUE..Integer.MAX_VALUE by wrapping, without error. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Any int computation whose true result exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE or is below Integer.MIN_VALUE: sums/products of large values, MAX_VALUE + 1, -Integer.MIN_VALUE, Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE).
wrong: Math.abs always returns a non-negative number. | right: Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) returns Integer.MIN_VALUE, which is negative.
